Avinox %1$s setup (%2$s kg total, %3$s rpm, %4$s W rider power)
%1$s: assist level %2$s · max. %3$s W · max. %4$s Nm
Max. watts = target in watts per kg of total weight × %1$s kg, rounded to 50 W and capped at what the motor and the mode allow.
Max. Nm = max. watts ÷ %1$s rpm × 9.55, rounded up to the next step of 5. That makes the watt limit available at your cadence.
Assist level = max. watts ÷ %1$s W rider power. The next higher level that delivers this assistance is chosen.
AUTO and TRAIL get a range: the upper value from the calculation, the lower one follows on from the mode below.
With all modes, the range steps (%1$s) deliberately keep the assist level below the watt limit. The strongest step uses the motor\'s maximum and gets one assist level in reserve.
Create the steps marked “new” as additional modes in the Avinox Ride app, with name and colour, and arrange them in this order.
On the flat, switch to one of the three lowest steps. That gives the most range.
In the strong modes, approach the motor overrun setting from a medium value. With a long overrun the bike keeps pushing in tight uphill corners.
Set the mode order in the app to ECO, AUTO, TRAIL, TURBO. Then you shift from weak to strong.
With real-time tuning you change the assist level from the handlebar while riding.
